angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 953,109 km at 67.71 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.7691 +/- 0.2115 mas (same row, RUWE 11.99): 67.71 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 1.37 solar radii from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: radius 1.37 solar radii (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684): 953,109 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.17 solar masses from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: mass 1.17 solar masses (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4600 K from Pecaut & Mamajek (2013, ApJS 208, 9), the online table's version 2022.04.16, row K4V, for SIMBAD's spectral type K4V(e): Teff (https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~emamajek/EEM_dwarf_UBVIJHK_colors_Teff.txt). Spin inclination 68 degrees and rotation period 5.7 d from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: rotation period 5.7 d and an axis 68 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Pecaut & Mamajek (2013, ApJS 208, 9), the online table's version 2022.04.16, row K4V, for SIMBAD's spectral type K4V(e): Teff (https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~emamajek/EEM_dwarf_UBVIJHK_colors_Teff.txt)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/tyc-6878-195-1.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.233, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, CD-26 13904: main object type **, Double or Multiple Star
